STYLE FILE · NO FACES REQUIRED

Ten styles that never draw a face

One sample frame per style. None depends on keeping a face on-model. Recommendation: Wooden Manikin for the people, animated in MiniMax, and Isotype Ledger for the numbers, animated in Remotion. Keep every word out of the art and add it in Remotion.

Wooden Manikin Recommended

Every person is the same faceless wooden drawing manikin. A character is a costume and a hat; poses do the acting.

Cost
1 costume sheet per character, then ~1 credit per shot
In MiniMax
Very good. Jointed wood moves plausibly: turning, reaching, sitting. One action per clip.
Best for
Careers, deals, any story where people do things
Guide
wooden-manikin.md

Isotype Ledger Pair with it

Everyone is the same pictogram. The outlaw gets one hat and the red. Numbers are rows of figures.

Cost
Code only, 0 credits
In MiniMax
Don't send it. Animate in Remotion; MiniMax would smear the crisp shapes.
Best for
Money, promotions, org charts, book interiors
Guide
isotype-ledger.md

Cut Paper Noir

Torn and cut paper, black does the work, the outlaw is a silhouette with dot eyes and a hatband.

Cost
~10–20 credits / episode
In MiniMax
Very good. Big flat shapes survive; slow pushes, smoke, falling paper.
Best for
Titles, thumbnails, covers, threat
Guide
cut-paper-noir.md

Neon Night New

The city at night told through wordless neon signs, rain and reflections. Figures are dark shapes from behind.

Cost
~1 credit per shot
In MiniMax
Excellent. Neon flicker, rain, ripples, a figure walking away.
Best for
Crime, Prohibition, mood, thumbnails
Guide
neon-night.md

Turned Away New

Flat Hopper-like rooms. People are only ever seen from behind; the back, hat and coat are the character.

Cost
~1 credit per shot
In MiniMax
Very good, but models like to turn him round. Prompt against it and cut those clips.
Best for
Biography, trials, prison, the exit interview
Guide
turned-away.md

Tin Toy Town New

Tabletop tin toys and plain wooden peg figures, shot like warm stop-motion.

Cost
~3 references per episode + 1 per shot
In MiniMax
Excellent. Wind-up cars drive off, trains run, doors swing; rigid toys keep their shape.
Best for
Heists, chases, empires, finance explainers
Guide
tin-toy-town.md

Travel Poster New

1950s screen-print posters. The place is the hero; people are tiny. Check eras: this test drew a 1973 tower.

Cost
~1 credit per shot
In MiniMax
Excellent. Clouds, smoke, water, a train or ship crossing.
Best for
Establishing shots, journeys, new cities, banners
Guide
travel-poster.md

Evidence Table

Seen from above. His objects and his sleeve tell the story; no head ever enters the frame.

Cost
~7–10 credits per outlaw, then reused
In MiniMax
Good for objects; hands may warp, keep hand moves short.
Best for
Deals, money, documents
Guide
evidence-table.md

Game Board

The career is a board game. The outlaw is a red pawn with a fedora; events are cards.

Cost
~1 credit per character + board pieces
In MiniMax
Fair. Slow pans, one token moving; exact hops in Remotion.
Best for
Journeys, rivalries, territory
Guide
game-board.md

Blueprint

Floor plans, routes and cutaways. People are tiny labelled scale figures; the plan is the hero.

Cost
Mostly code, 1–3 credits / episode
In MiniMax
Don't send it. Draw-on lines and routes are exact in Remotion.
Best for
Heists, escapes, tunnels, ships
Guide
blueprint.md
Isotype and Blueprint were drawn in code (0 credits). The other frames are single Recraft test images (1 credit each), not tuned. All figures and plans are illustrative, not sourced. The Travel Poster test shows a modern skyline in a 1920s scene: prompts must name the year.
